result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position by eliminating liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. However, it is not minimal: it removes the original ten-day grace period and makes interest Vendor’s “sole remedy,” which could unintentionally waive recovery, suspension, termination, or other contractual remedies for nonpayment. The Section 7.3 language also leaves unclear when interest begins if withheld amounts are ultimately found due. Although generally professional, the clause should preserve the grace period and limit only late-payment charges rather than all remedies.
